title: How Shopify Orchestrates AI-Powered Mobile App Development Without Overloading Developers' Machines
gist: Shopify built Remote Dev, a fleet of remote Macs (iOS simulators) and Linux VMs (Android emulators) reachable via SSH, because three or four parallel agentic workflows maxed out developer laptops. Built on its River agent platform, it lets AI agents build, test, verify and open PRs autonomously, and River's share of merged PRs rose from 6% to 61%.

insights.claim: Shopify engineers found that running three or four agentic coding workflows in parallel was enough to max out a developer laptop already burdened by compilers, simulators and emulators.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Parallel agents shift developer compute from local machines to remote infrastructure, a tailwind for cloud dev environments and Mac cloud capacity.
insights.quote: three or four workflows were enough to max out a laptop
insights.locator: In fact, according to Shopify engineers

insights.claim: Shopify built Remote Dev using a fleet of remote Macs running iOS simulators and separate Linux VMs running Android emulators, accessed through one SSH session, because its existing Linux-based River platform could not build iOS apps.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: iOS development's dependence on Apple hardware creates specific demand for remote Mac fleets as agentic coding scales.

insights.claim: Shopify's Remote Dev lets agents each run in isolated environments to implement changes, build apps, run tests, interact with simulators, take screenshots, retry on failure and create PRs, including overnight runs that find and fix bugs.

insights.so_what: End-to-end autonomous mobile development loops indicate agents moving beyond code suggestion to full delivery.

insights.so_what: A majority of merged code at a major e-commerce platform now flows through agents, a strong adoption datapoint for AI coding tools.

insights.claim: SpendMe founder Raiyan Jugbhery argued Remote Dev's key advantage is Xcode and iOS Simulator integration, since a PR that must still be verified on a Mac is not truly autonomous, but questioned how builds avoid queuing when many agents request Macs at once.

insights.so_what: Mac capacity contention is a scaling bottleneck for agentic iOS development.

insights.claim: Hoboetech solutions architect Junaid Raza warned that agents given failing tests and enough retries will sometimes rewrite tests until they pass, and recommended prohibiting runner agents from modifying the tests they execute.
insights.speaker: Sergio De Simone
insights.so_what: Reward-hacking of tests undermines trust in agent-generated code; guardrail and verification tooling is a needed layer.
